note: Attacker-controlled input is null-terminated on the heap; its full length is derived here and later misused as half_length.
When sum < 20 (only 4 printable chars in the PoC), the full string length (64) is passed as the half_length argument, not half of anything.
Only a lower-bound check; half_length = 64 passes it, so the vulnerable doubling and read proceed.
Doubles half_length to 128 with no upper-bound validation against the buffer size, contradicting the comment that half_length is under 10; this makes the subsequent index exceed the heap allocation.
Guard only requires the string to be at least 40 bytes; it never bounds the idx argument (128) against the 65-byte heap buffer.
Reads input[128], 64 bytes past the null terminator and far beyond the 65-byte heap allocation, causing an ASan heap-buffer-overflow read.
